title: The Hesitant Thief
logline: A servant and his friend are robbing the house when the owner knocks; the servant points his friend to the back door by the well, and the friend finds the open door but refuses to leave until he has found the well, so he is caught.
moral: When the way out is in front of you, take it; fussing over a detail that does not matter costs you the chance.
tone: Door-slamming farce: quick, light, built on one stubborn idea repeated while the knocking grows; no real menace.

beats.summary: The servant knows every door: FRONT DOOR left, BACK DOOR right.
He and a friend agree to steal from the house.
One night the family is out and the two fill sacks.
They believe they have plenty of time (hourglass full).
Loud knocking: the owner is back.
Escape by the back door, by the well: the fatal extra detail.
The back door is open and the way out is clear.
No well beside it, so he stops.
He runs back to ask where the well is.
How can I leave without seeing it? He plants his feet.
The knocking grows and the owner gets angry.
Begged and pushed, he still asks about the missing well.
The front door opens and the owner walks in.
He runs at last, too late, and is caught on the threshold.
I found the door, but I could not find the well!
The thief goes to the judge and the sacks stay in the house.

props.description: Lumpy brown sack about 110 wide x 130 tall with a fill field 0..1 (empty rag to full with bumps) and an optional object poking out. Planned by KD-013.

subtitles.ar: عمل خادم في بيت رجل غني، وكان يعرف كل غرفة وكل باب فيه.|لكنه اتفق مع صديق له على السرقة.|كان الصديق يدخل البيت عندما يخرج أصحابه،|ثم يبيعان ما يأخذانه ويقسمان المال.
subtitles.en: A servant worked in a wealthy man’s house and knew every room and every door.|But he made a plan to steal with a friend.|His friend came inside whenever the owners went out,|and they sold what they took and divided the money.

subtitles.ar: وفي ليلة، خرج أهل البيت لزيارة أقاربهم.|جاء الصديق، وبدأ الاثنان يجمعان أشياء ثمينة في أكياس.|كانا يظنان أن أمامهما وقتًا طويلًا، وأن أحدًا لن يعود قريبًا.
subtitles.en: One night, the family went out to visit relatives.|The friend arrived, and the two began putting valuable things into bags.|They thought they had plenty of time and that nobody would return soon.

subtitles.ar: فجأة، سمعا طرقًا قويًا على الباب الأمامي.|صاح صاحب البيت من الخارج: «افتحوا الباب!»|خاف الرجلان. قال الخادم لصديقه:|«اهرب بسرعة من الباب الخلفي، عند البئر!» وأشار إليه بيده.
subtitles.en: Suddenly, they heard loud knocking at the front door.|The owner shouted from outside, “Open the door!”|Both men were terrified. The servant told his friend,|“Quick! Escape through the back door by the well!” and pointed the way.

subtitles.ar: ركض اللص إلى الخلف، ووجد الباب المفتوح.|لكنه لم يرَ بئرًا بجانبه.|عاد مسرعًا إلى الخادم وقال:|«وجدت الباب، لكن أين البئر التي تحدثت عنها؟»
subtitles.en: The thief ran to the back and found the open door.|But he saw no well beside it.|He hurried back to the servant and said,|“I found the door, but where is the well you mentioned?”

subtitles.ar: قال الخادم: «لم أذكر البئر إلا لتعرف مكان الباب!|إذا وجدته، فاخرج فورًا!»|رد اللص: «ولكنك قلت إن البئر هناك.|بحثت عنها ولم أجدها. كيف أخرج دون أن أراها؟»
subtitles.en: “I mentioned the well only to help you find the door!” the servant said.|“Once you find it, go out immediately!”|The thief replied, “But you said the well was there.|I looked and could not find it. How can I leave without seeing it?”

subtitles.ar: ازدادت أصوات الطرق على الباب، وبدأ صاحب البيت يغضب.|توسل الخادم إلى صديقه: «انسَ البئر!|الباب أمامك، والنجاة قريبة!»|لكن اللص ظل يسأل عن البئر المفقودة.
subtitles.en: The knocking grew louder, and the owner became angry.|The servant begged his friend, “Forget the well!|The door is in front of you, and you can still escape!”|But the thief kept asking about the missing well.

subtitles.ar: وأخيرًا، فُتح الباب الأمامي، ودخل صاحب البيت.|رأى الأكياس المملوءة بأشيائه، ثم رأى الرجلين يتجادلان.|حاول اللص أن يهرب، لكن الوقت كان قد فات،|فأمسك به صاحب البيت.
subtitles.en: At last, the front door opened, and the owner came inside.|He saw bags filled with his belongings and then the two men arguing.|The thief tried to run, but it was too late,|and the owner caught him.

subtitles.ar: سأل صاحب البيت: «لماذا لم تهرب من الباب الخلفي؟»|قال اللص في حيرة: «وجدت الباب، لكنني لم أجد البئر!»|لم يصدق الرجل ما سمعه.|وأخذ اللص إلى الحاكم، وبقيت الأكياس في البيت.
subtitles.en: “Why did you not escape through the back door?” the owner asked.|The thief answered, confused, “I found the door, but I could not find the well!”|The owner could hardly believe it.|He took the thief to the judge, and the bags stayed in the house.

new_assets.name: palaceHall (variant merchantHouse)
new_assets.description: The planned merchant house interior, built here as a 1800-wide side cutaway with a street on the left, a yard on the right and two working doors (open 0..1), day and night palettes. Reusable for any house, robbery or guest story.
new_assets.implementation: One function per layer baked with bake(): sky/nightCity backdrop, walls as black-bordered rects with Ben-Day fills (hp dots), shelf, carpet, lamp (lamp swing drawn live), yard wall, palm (trunk rect + five leaf wedges), gate arch. Doors drawn live: a rect whose width is 16 + 94 * open, hinged on the wall, with a ring handle; shake = small rotation about the hinge. Coordinates are given in sets[0].

new_assets.name: person costume presets (servant)
new_assets.description: Adds a 'servant' preset to the planned person costume layer (flat cap, short tunic, sash). This film also uses the planned 'merchant' and 'lady' presets.
new_assets.implementation: Optional costume field on person(): draws headwear, beard and robe shapes over the existing body after the torso and before the arms, so arm IK, gestures, gaze and blinks are unchanged. Default (no costume) must render exactly as now; run the regression test.

new_assets.name: sack, coin, valuables
new_assets.description: Sack with fill 0..1, coin and four shelf valuables plus a broom (see props). Sack and coin are the drawings planned by KD-013.
new_assets.implementation: Flat paths with black outline and one dot shade each; the sack is a closed bezier whose bumps scale with fill, neck tied with a short line.

new_assets.name: well
new_assets.description: Above-ground well icon with ghost and mark options (see props); the story's running gag object. Reusable for village and yard scenes.
new_assets.implementation: Blocks as rects in two offset rows, two post rects, a triangle roof, a line and a small bucket trapezoid. ghost:true strokes the same paths with setLineDash([10, 8]) in blue and no fill.

new_assets.name: hourglass
new_assets.description: Panel-space time meter (see props) keyed: appears 36.16 at 1.0; 55.4 starts to run; 0.75 at 65.2; 0.6 at 83.5; 0.4 at 103.5; 0.25 at 111.3; 0.05 at 123.1; 0 and red at 140.0-141.5; hidden after 146.
new_assets.implementation: Two triangles for the glass, sand as clipped rects by fill, a 3 px stream line when the value is falling; drawn after the world and before S.finish, in panel coordinates.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: The planned generic thought cloud, used for the friend's fixed idea (well with ? or x) and the servant's speech balloon icons.
new_assets.implementation: Cloud outline from overlapping circles with a white fill and black stroke, three shrinking bubbles to the head, a draw callback for the contents; pops in with settleTo.

new_assets.name: inset circle
new_assets.description: The planned round picture-in-picture (r 120, top left of the panel) showing the bulging front door during 116.8-123.0.
new_assets.implementation: Clip a circle in panel space, draw the world again with a second camera (x 430, y 720, zoom 0.9), stroke a fat black ring; open and close with a radius ramp.

new_assets.name: person kneel / sit
new_assets.description: Planned kneel and sit fields: the servant kneels to beg (111.3-116.8), the friend sits on his sack (35.0-44.2).
new_assets.implementation: kneel 0..1 lowers the hips by up to 70 and draws the shins flat on the floor; sit 0..1 lowers the hips by 60 with thighs forward. Both keep the torso, arms and head code unchanged.

new_assets.name: runInPlace
new_assets.description: Comic wind-up: the legs cycle at full run amplitude for about 1.2 s with no travel, dust building behind, then release into a real run; also used for the legs running in the air after the collar grab.
new_assets.implementation: Return {ph, amp} from time instead of distance (ph = 22 * (t - t0), amp 1) and blend to walk(TX, t) at release so the phase is continuous.

new_assets.name: flush
new_assets.description: Planned anger flush 0..1 with steam puffs, for the owner at 110.06.
new_assets.implementation: Red Ben-Day dots clipped to the face shape, rising from the chin with the value; two small white puffs with black outline drifting up from the turban.

owner_questions: The script does not say what happens to the servant: by default he is not arrested on screen; he hides behind a sack and at the end sheepishly puts a candlestick back on the shelf.
Addition beyond the script at 119.96-121.3: the friend walks out into the yard, looks under a flowerpot and comes back inside; default is to keep it because it shows that he could have left.
An hourglass meter with the invented labels PLENTY OF TIME (38.4) and TOO LATE! (141.5) runs through the film; default is to keep it.
The judge is not shown; by default the owner walks the friend out of the front door under an arrow labelled TO THE JUDGE.
The owner's wife is added as a silent companion (the script says the family went out); default is to include her leaving, waiting at the door and peeking in.
Invented lettering by default: KNOCK! KNOCK!, OPEN UP!, ZOOM!, NO WELL?, GO!, BANG! BANG!, CREAK..., TOO LATE!, GOTCHA!, and the labels FRONT DOOR, BACK DOOR, WAY OUT, MY THINGS!.
implementation_notes: World 1800 x 1230 with the floor at y 900 (the template uses 1000 wide; set WW = 1800 and clamp the camera to it). Minimum zoom 1.0 so the view never exceeds the world height.
The whole hall (x 350..1350) fits one zoom 1.0 shot at camera x 850: use it whenever both doors must be read together (6.9, 62.5, 133.6, 161.3).

Knocks are narrated, not heard: there is no knock sound effect because every knock falls inside a spoken word. Show them with door motion, impact stars, lamp swing and panel-only shake. Sound effects are only the four listed (21.85, 136.9, 145.3, 166.6), master 0.6.

Knock rhythm: drive door hits from one list. S5: 43.08, 46.06, 46.74, 47.52, then a hit every 0.9 s in the background while the camera is inside (soft, 2 px) up to 103.5; S11: every 0.55 s from 103.52 to 107.9 with rising amplitude; none after 108.0 except the bulges in the inset (116.9, 118.0, 119.1, 120.2, 121.3, 122.4); silence from 123.08.
The back door stays open from 68.3 to the end of the film. Never close it: the open exit in the background of every later shot is the point.
The friend never looks frightened between 74.86 and 136.7. Keep his face calm and reasonable; all panic belongs to the servant.
Use LIFE.t = t for automatic blinks; add hand blinks where a lid is set; noBlink during the held shocks (44.2-45.3, 136.75-137.2).
Arms that must read at phone size (pointing at the door, thumb over the shoulder, the X) use aL/aR arm angles, not hand targets.
Positions: packing spot servant x 700, friend x 820; sacks x 760 and x 860; argument spot S8-S10 servant x 720, friend x 850; S12 servant x 1100, friend x 1200; catch at x 1270.
Subtitles: chunk marks are in subtitles[]; copy them to chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt and verify by program against the script.
warnings: The planned assets merchant and lady costume presets, thoughtCloud, inset circle, kneel/sit and flush do not exist in Library yet; if another story builds them first, reuse them.
Edge-on doors must still read as doors: give each a strong frame, a ring handle on both faces and a visible swing; check a still at 46.1 and 68.6.
The inset circle (top left) and the hourglass (top right) share the top of the panel in S12: keep both clear of the thought cloud, which then sits top centre.
Sky presets: check that sky() has a night option; otherwise use the nightCity backdrop behind the street and a navy fill with stars over the yard.
